***Abstract*****—  DodgerWin is a new solution that allows Dodger fan, who are not available to watch a Dodger game, to see how their favorite team performs. The application will alert them about LA Dodger’s performance and discounted meal at Panda Express when Dodger won a game.** 


1. Introduction \- What are we building?

DodgerWin is a web application that would monitor and display the Los Angeles Dodgers at home victories that would fulfill the criteria for a discounted Panda Express mail. When a Dodger’s victory is announced,  the user will be notified and a Panda Express discount code will be sent to the user through their mobile SMS.   
The project will be built with Python and hosted on AWS. The application’s database will contain a user phone number, which will raise the need for security and risk management. 

2. Project Goals 

To make sure that the application runs as intended to provide a smooth experience for the user, there are goals that played as our guide to develop this project. Some of the goals that we want to achieve are: 

* Have the application run smoothly on cloud through Amazon Web Service (AWS)   
* Create a functional system that accurately checks if the Dodgers win at home and display the correct discount code  
* Successfully send out notifications the moment both criteria are checked for discount   
* Keep our database personal info database hidden and out of reach from intruders by encrypting the data in the event of breach   
* Implement countermeasurement to prevent attackers from spamming large numbers into our database   
* Ensure numbers enrolled in database pertain to the individual interested in the web application

3. Technology Stack for The Project 

The technology stack will help us define the blueprint of our application, how the project is built, what is the cost, and what is the time spent to produce. 

1. *AWS Services*

One of the main goals for our web application is to run it smoothly on the cloud. With AWS, the goal will be achieved easily thanks to the plethora of services that Amazon provides on their cloud service. Some of the services that we consider are extended but not limited to: 

* Lambda \+ EventBridge: Lambda will help with the game-check and notification logic when needed and EventBridge triggers it on a schedule    
* SNS \+ Twilio: SNS will fans out alerts and Twilio will send the actual text message the moment the discount criteria are met  
* Cognito: will be used to manage user and authentication   
* KMS: Manages the encryption keys to protect the phone number so the data is unreadable in a breach  
* Secret Manager: Store API Keys and Twilio credentials safely  
* IAM: enforce least privilege  
* CloudTrail \+ CloutWatch: CloudTrail help logs every account action for auditing while CloudWatch help handling monitoring and alerts  
* S3 \+ Route 53: S3 will hosts the static React frontend through CloudFront and Route 53 provides DNS and custom domain

4. Application Architecture 

The application architecture helps our team structuring the design and organizing the application interactions between components, data, user interfaces, and external system interaction. 

1. Serverless Architecture 

DodgerWin is a serverless application that is built with security-layered architecture.  Each layer was built to ensure the application worked well in a  serverless framework. The structure is visualized as shown in Figure 1\.

1) Entry layer (Edge)  
* Internet → CloudFront → AWS WAF: All user traffic enters through CloudFront, then WAF filters out malicious requests such as SQL Injection before anything else see them   
* From WAF, traffic goes two ways: to the Website frontend and to API Gateway for backend calls  
2) API Gateway   
* Acts as the single front door to the backend. It will route requests to the right Lambda function inside the private VPC subnet   
3) Private VPC Subnet (Application Layer)

   There group of Lambda lives here, shielded from direct internet access 

1) Game Pipeline: Game Result Lambda \-\> Get Promotion Lambda → Notification Lambda. This chain checks whether the Dodgers won at home, retrieves the Panda Express discount code, then triggers notifications  
2) Enlist Subscriber Lambda: handles signup requests from the website and writes the user’s phone number to the database   
3) Admin Service Lambda: Handles administrative functions, authenticated through Cognito  
4) Data and External Service  
* DynamoDB \+ AWS KMS: Encrypted storage for subscriber phone numbers and game/promo data. Enlist Subscriber and Notification Lambdas read from or write to it  
* Send SMS: Notification lambda sends texts to subscribers once both discount criteria are met  
* Cognito \+MFA: Protects the admin function with multi-factor authentication, so only authorized staff can use it

Fig. 1  Architectural diagram of DodgerWin 

2.  Three Tier Architecture

The Three Tier Architecture is an application architecture that helps organize applications into three logical and physical tiers. The benefit of applying three-tier is the independence, in which each tier can be updated or scaled as needed without impacting the other tiers\[1\]. The following is the three-tier architecture for DodgerWin:

1)  Presentation Tier

   This tier will contain everything that the user will be interacting with. The following are the tech stack that we will use for this tier. The list is extended but not limited to: 

* React \- for signup form, OTP entry, and page showing the Dodgers win status and discount code  
* S3 \- for hosting the built react files as static site  
* CloudFront \- Serves the site oliver HTTPS from edge locations, so it’s fast and the S3 bucket stays private  
* Route 53 \- DNS, so users reach the site at our domain   
* AWS WAF \- Attached to CloudFront to filter SQL injection, XSS, and bots  
* CAPTCHA \- to slowdown bots   
2) Application Tier

   This tier represents the application’s logic. It controls decisions, validates input, and communicates with third-party services. The following list is the tech stacks applied to this tier. The stack is extended but not limited to: 

   Lambda: for running Python code in serverless, one function per job 

   EventBridge: for schedule trigger Game Result Lambda after games

   Cognito: to authenticates admin users before Admin lambda runs 

   Secret Manager: to Hold sport API key and Twilio credentials which Lambdas fetch at runtime 

3) Data Tier 

   This tier stores the data of the whole application. Some of the stacks for this tier include:

   DynamoDB: for storing subscriber phone number, verification state, and game/promo records

   KMS: Encryption keys for the table, so data is unreadable if someone get at the storage

6. Work in Progress

We are still working on inputting features that we feel are both necessary for both functionality and for a more feature complete website.

For functionality:

* Unsubscribe Lambda: It's important for users to have the freedom to unsubscribe whenever they choose and to have the database reflect that decision.  
* Text/SMS Notifications: Something we’ve been looking into but haven’t found a solid solution to. We seen that it might be costly to run a service like this, and for the sake of saving money, we’re going to continue running the site with just sending out emails and see if we can find something suitable for this project  
* Main Messaging Lambda: While the system currently works with sending an email to one email/phone number, we want it to be able to send updates to all emails or phone numbers attached. This means we will likely need to use a database for the phone numbers and emails, and have the lambda iterate through the database and send a message to each one  
* Admin Service Lambda: This would give us direct control over the information that is presented in the site, in the event of an incorrect game result, changing the discount shown on the site, or checking on operations as they should be occurring automatically.  
* Security layer to defend our application from bot spamming and SQL Injection 

More features:

* AI winning statistic bot: Something fun for the site would be a bot that gives the probability for the current/next Dodger game. Users can then see when to expect another notification when they do win.  
* Another kind of promotion: There are other promotions that happen when the Dodgers win, outside of the Panda Express discount. This way, we can better use this platform to help users get discounts for other things.

7. Challenges of the Team 

The project is a good opportunity for us to learn more about developing an application in the Cloud. With this new knowledge about Cloud Computing, we also face some challenges due to our lack of experiences. 

One challenge that the team faces is calculating the cost for the project. Since AWS charges for each instance of EC2 and time to host an application, as a group of students, we are not ready for spending real money on a classroom-level project. Another thing that costs money is sport data, since some sports channels locked their API and metadata through a paywall. Though we have found free alternatives for the API and some way to manage the cost of AWS, this is a valuable lesson for us to learn. I believe in the real industry that we will be a part of, cost management is a required skill. Through this challenge, we learned how to discuss the cost of the project in the planning phase, and how to be flexible in cost management during the development phase. 

8. Reflection

The project gave us a good learning experience. We got to learn more about AWS and the benefits of working in the Cloud. We are also learning how to build an application with three-tier architecture. At an interpersonal level, we learned more about teamworking. Though there are challenges and work to be done for the upcoming work, we believe that this current stage of the project is a valuable lesson for us to perform better in the next stage of this project until we finish it.
